vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kokoro-agent-voices
Version: 1.0.0

The `scripts/speak.py` file contains a shell injection vulnerability. The script uses `os.system(f"afplay {out}")` to play generated audio, where the `out` variable (the output WAV file path) is directly derived from user-controlled input (`--output` argument). This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary shell commands, leading to potential remote code execution. While the skill's stated purpose and network activity (Hugging Face model download) appear legitimate, this vulnerability makes the skill suspicious.

llm.summary: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose (local Kokoro TTS), requests no secrets, and its runtime actions (downloading a model from Hugging Face and synthesizing WAV audio locally) match the description.

dimensions.detail: Name/description: local Kokoro TTS. Required binaries (python3, espeak-ng) and the included script align with running a local Python TTS pipeline. Minor inconsistency: the script does not directly call the espeak-ng binary, so declaring espeak-ng as a required binary may be unnecessary or a leftover from packaging instructions, but this does not contradict the overall purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts/speak.py restrict actions to listing voices/agents, downloading the Kokoro model from Hugging Face, generating local WAV output, and optionally playing audio via a platform player. The skill does not read arbitrary user files, environment secrets, or transmit data to unexpected third-party endpoints beyond Hugging Face (model download).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only plus one script). The runtime downloads the Kokoro model from the Hugging Face Hub (~350MB) on first run — a standard, expected behavior for model-based local inference but a notable network and disk cost. The Hugging Face source is a well-known release host.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials and the code does not access secrets or unrelated config paths. Dependency requirements (kokoro, soundfile, numpy, huggingface_hub) are proportional to local TTS functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false; the skill does not request persistent platform privileges or modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It writes generated WAV files to user-specified paths (default /tmp) and caches model files via huggingface_hub as expected.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: run Kokoro TTS locally and download the model from Hugging Face on first use. Things to consider before installing: (1) The model download is large (~350MB) and requires outbound network access to huggingface.co; plan for disk and bandwidth. (2) The script lists espeak-ng as a required binary but does not invoke it directly — verify whether you actually need espeak-ng in your environment. (3) The included shebang references a user-specific virtualenv path (likely an author artifact); run the script with your Python interpreter or inside a dedicated virtualenv. (4) The script may write WAV files (default /tmp) and can call an OS audio player (afplay) when --play is used; run it in an environment where those effects are acceptable. If you need stronger isolation, run the skill in a sandboxed or ephemeral VM/container and review or pin the Python package dependencies (kokoro, huggingface_hub, numpy, soundfile) before use.
